structures.name: Skin, with simulated coat
structures.sourceLabel: outer surface of all source labels
structures.description: The outer surface of the union of all Digimouse labels, carried into the stance and smoothed. Moved to the simulated standing posture by rotating limb segments about joints read from the source CT. Soft parts that would then stand outside the simulated skin or paws are drawn in under them. The shanks and forearms are simulated shapes whose radii are measured from the limb tissue and limited to a slender limb, because the scanned shanks lay pressed flat, the scanned forearms end in a blunt mass round the wrists, and the images end at the hind feet. The fur drawn on the surface is simulated, because the specimen is a nude mouse, and so are the colours of the skin under it and of the ears, tail, paws and nose that go with each coat.
basis: Dogdas B, Stout D, Chatziioannou AF, Leahy RM. Digimouse: a 3D whole body mouse atlas from CT and cryosection data. Phys Med Biol 2007. doi:10.1088/0031-9155/52/3/003
Cook MJ. The Anatomy of the Laboratory Mouse. Academic Press, 1965; web edition at https://www.informatics.jax.org/cookbook/

structures.name: Wall of the abdomen
structures.description: Simulated. One sheet for the wall of the belly and flanks, between the ribs and the pelvis, so that the abdomen can be opened as a layer. In the mouse, Carlson and Chakkalakal find the linea alba and peritoneum under the skin at the midline, and muscle to each side of it, and here the middle line is drawn pale. The sheet is taken from the simulated body surface at a chosen depth. Its depth, the width of its middle line and the direction of its fibres are estimates, and it is not measured. It is drawn faintly, except at the bench, where it is opened.
basis: Carlson MA, Chakkalakal D. Tensile properties of the murine ventral vertical midline incision. PLoS One. 2011;6(9):e24212. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0024212

structures.name: Meningeal lymphatic vessels
structures.description: Simulated. Fine vessels beside the dural sinuses, going on down the neck. Louveau et al. find functional lymphatic vessels lining the dural sinuses in mice, connected to the deep cervical lymph nodes. Their courses and widths are estimates. Not measured from this specimen.
basis: Louveau A, Smirnov I, Keyes TJ, et al. Structural and functional features of central nervous system lymphatic vessels. Nature 2015;523(7560):337-41. doi:10.1038/nature14432

structures.name: Vomer
structures.description: Simulated. A thin plate in the midline, low in the septum of the nose. In the mouse it meets the premaxilla at a suture, and its Y-shaped wings lie on each side of the lower part of the septal cartilage, as Kim et al. describe; here it is a simple plate without wings. The CT does not separate it, and its size and place are estimates. Not measured from this specimen.
basis: Kim BS, Shin HR, Kim HJ, Yoon H, Cho YD, Choi KY, Choi JY, Kim WJ, Ryoo HM. Septal chondrocyte hypertrophy contributes to midface deformity in a mouse model of Apert syndrome. Sci Rep. 2021;11(1):7979. doi:10.1038/s41598-021-87260-5

structures.name: Ethmoid
structures.description: Simulated. A plate between the olfactory bulbs and the nasal cavities, with a thin plate going forward in the midline. In the mouse the cribriform plate of this bone has holes in it, separates the cranial and nasal cavities and is shaped to the rounded front of the olfactory bulbs, as Norwood et al. describe, and its perpendicular plate lies against the septal cartilage, as Kim et al. describe; here the plate is flat and has no holes. The CT does not separate it, and its size and place are estimates. Not measured from this specimen.
basis: Norwood JN, Zhang Q, Card D, Craine A, Ryan TM, Drew PJ. Anatomical basis and physiological role of cerebrospinal fluid transport through the murine cribriform plate. eLife. 2019;8:e44278. doi:10.7554/eLife.44278

structures.name: Lacrimal bones
structures.description: Simulated. A small bone at the front of each orbit, as labelled on the skull from above in Cook figure 11, which meets the frontal bone and the frontal process of the maxilla, as Martinez-Abadias et al. give it in the newborn mouse. The CT does not separate it, and its size and place are estimates. Not measured from this specimen.

structures.description: Simulated. Tarsals, metatarsals and phalanges by the counts in Hummel et al., drawn as simple shafts, because the source images end at the hind feet. Not measured from this specimen.
basis: Cook MJ. The Anatomy of the Laboratory Mouse. Academic Press, 1965; web edition at https://www.informatics.jax.org/cookbook/

limitations: This is a constructed model and not a measurement of a living mouse. Each structure states whether it is source-labelled, traced from the source images or simulated.
The standing posture is simulated: the specimen was scanned spread flat, postmortem and frozen, and its limbs were rotated about their joints to an estimated stance.
Simulated structures follow published anatomical descriptions and are not measured from this specimen or any other.
Anatomical orientation, laterality and physical calibration remain unverified.

specimen.description: Measured layers from one 28 g normal nude male mouse, with a simulated posture and simulated layers. The coat is simulated, because the specimen is hairless.
